title: Making Low Peptone NGM for Imaging Plates
author: Priota Islam
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.2rcgd2w

steps.title: Prepare Pre-autoclave Reagents
steps.instruction: Measure all pre-autoclave reagents and add them to clean flasks from the glass kitchen, ensuring a new weighing boat and spatula are used for each reagent (note: cholesterol is stored in the fridge).

substeps.instruction: Label the flask with autoclave tape as 'Low peptone NGM Rm 5020'.

steps.title: Set Up and Run Autoclave
steps.instruction: Prepare the autoclave machine and run the 'media' program.

substeps.instruction: Fill the autoclave's probe bottle (same size as the largest bottle used) with water and place the temperature probe inside.
Fill the autoclave with water until it reaches the grill.
Check that the waste flask is not too full.
Place bottles in the autoclave, ensuring caps are not screwed completely.
Select the 'media' program and press START.
Allow for approximately 2 hours for a 500ml bottle or 2.5 hours for bottles 1L or larger.

steps.title: Add Post-autoclave Reagents and Pour
steps.instruction: Remove the flask from the autoclave using gloves and prepare for pouring.

substeps.instruction: Allow agar to cool to approximately 55°C (cool enough to hold for a second with a gloved hand).
Mix well, avoiding excessive shaking to prevent air bubbles.
Pour onto imaging plates quickly to prevent blocking the tubings.
If not poured immediately, keep the bottle on a waterbath set to 60°C.
